content:
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to be unveiled next week, with the latest reports further revealing details about the "mechanical aperture" camera feature and improved vapor chamber configuration of these two flagship phones.

Below are the new features of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max disclosed by Mark Gurman.

Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman published his latest predictions today, discussing the new iPhones scheduled for launch on September 9.

Although most of the report covers known features, there are still several new details worth noting.

For example, Apple will add a new "mechanical aperture" camera feature to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the smaller iPhone 18 Pro may also be equipped with this feature.

Although this camera upgrade has been reported multiple times and is also referred to as a "variable aperture," the public has not fully understood its actual purpose. Gurman pointed out today that this feature can be used for "precise adjustment of light and depth of field control."

In addition, the new report also mentioned that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will bring "longer-lasting battery life, as well as an improved vapor chamber to help prevent overheating."

Longer battery life was already expected, and confirmation is undoubtedly good news; however, the improved vapor chamber is newly disclosed information.

Apple first adopted the vapor chamber design in the iPhone 17 Pro last year, and it appears the company is now ready to launch the second-generation version.

Finally, Gurman stated that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be equipped with "the self-developed C2 modem chip." Although this is not a new rumor, it is worth mentioning because some reports had indicated that Apple would continue to use Qualcomm's modem chips this year.

To learn more about the expected configurations of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, please read our related reports.
